title: Test 1
description: A conversation between Sophia and Ethan about visiting a local art exhibition
instructions: Each conversation is followed by a set of multiple-choice questions.
Choose the best answer for each question.

passages.title: Choosing a Guest Speaker for a Business Seminar
passages.setting: A woman is asking a gym staff member about fitness class options.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: So, we need to decide who we want as our keynote speaker for the seminar next month.

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: I’d suggest Susan Lee. She spoke at last year’s event and got great feedback.

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: She was excellent, but maybe we should bring in someone new this time? What about Daniel Reaves?

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: He’s the marketing strategist, right? He’s good, but I’m not sure if students will find his talk engaging.

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: Actually, I’ve heard he includes interactive activities. That might be more appealing this year.

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: That’s a good point. We also haven’t had a speaker from the tech sector in a while. He could bring a fresh angle.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: Okay, let’s go with Daniel, then. I’ll reach out to confirm his availability.

questions.question: What is the group trying to decide?

choices.text: What the seminar topic should be
Who the guest speaker should be

questions.question: What is one reason they choose Daniel Reaves?

choices.text: He gave a great speech last year

passages.title: Deciding on a Team Building Activity
passages.setting: A man is speaking with a gallery staff member about a new exhibit.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: Alright, team. We have the afternoon off next Friday for a team-building activity. What are our options?

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: Escape room, hiking, or maybe a pottery class?

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: Escape room sounds fun, but not everyone enjoys puzzles.

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: True. Hiking might be more relaxed, and it’s free.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: What about pottery? It’s indoors, good for any weather, and a new experience for most of us.

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: I actually love that idea. Plus, we can take something home.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: Pottery it is, then. I’ll book the studio.

questions.question: What activity do they agree on?
What is one reason they choose pottery?

passages.title: Organizing a Class Group Project
passages.setting: A man is speaking with a gallery staff member about a new exhibit.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: So, we need to divide the tasks for our group presentation. I can handle the visuals and PowerPoint slides.

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: Great. I’ll take care of the research section. I’ve already gathered some articles.

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: I’m happy to present the final part and do the speaking.

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: Awesome. That leaves the introduction.

conversation.name: Speaker 2
conversation.text: I can do that too, since I’m already deep into the research.

conversation.name: Speaker 3
conversation.text: That works. When should we rehearse?

conversation.name: Speaker 1
conversation.text: How about Wednesday evening?
